title: integer census verification run
note: Every structure and operation fact on integer's census page, as executable vectors; the border facts filed away on that page are OUT of scope. Integer is the first page needing PER-LANGUAGE probe text: the largest-value spelling differs everywhere, so a probe's body lives in templates/<lang>.integer.pre as a named function and the vector carries only the call. The unbounded camp (python, ruby) is probed against the fixed-width camp's own guarantees -- 2^63-1 arithmetic -- so the two camps are answering the same question.

expectation_alphabet.<any>: any result acceptable -- the language guarantees nothing here (the owner's cpp signed-overflow ruling made executable)
expectation_alphabet.<raise:*>: must refuse at runtime, by any name; the exact name is kept in results/ and quoted in the log

conventions.opaque_helpers: Every probe routes its operands through an op() identity helper so the value is a RUNTIME value. Without this, go refuses a constant overflow or a constant zero divisor at build time, and several compilers answer the question themselves -- both different questions from the one the census asks.

language_status.typescript: active (tsc -> node); the census claims it has NO integer, so its integer facts run as the float-only camp
language_status.csharp: blocked-deliberate (no toolchain in the container; not pursued)
language_status.rust-release: active (-O build -- overflow UNCHECKED; the record-both-modes rule)
language_status.dart: active (native, `dart run`) -- SDK installed 2026-08-14 once .googleapis.com egress went live
language_status.dart-web: active (`dart compile js` -> node); the second half of record-both-modes for dart
language_status.swift: not run (bonus language, outside the census's 11 targets; the heavy pages were kept proportionate)

facts.description: + - * agree exactly while no width limit is hit. The census believes this 11/11.
Comparison (< <= == >) agrees exactly on in-range values.
Decimal printing of an in-range integer agrees.

What values an 'integer' can hold. Three camps: fixed-width (rust go java csharp kotlin cpp dart php), unbounded (python ruby), and NO INTEGER AT ALL (typescript: number is the float, exact only to 2^53). Probe a is 2^53+1, the first value the float camp cannot hold; probe b is the 64-bit maximum. Probe c is the unbounded camp's own claim (2^70 exactly). Probes d and e are the developer-chosen-width and unsigned-exists sub-fractures. a and b live in their own program because a literal that cannot be represented is a COMPILE-time question in some modes.

Overflow: what happens when + - * exceed the width. The census's five behaviours: wrap silently (java kotlin csharp go dart-native cpp-UNSIGNED); undefined behaviour (cpp SIGNED); mode-dependent (rust debug PANICS / release wraps; dart native wraps / web behaves as floats); become a float (php); grow (python ruby). Probe a is each language's guaranteed spelling of 'largest value plus one', through opaque runtime values so no compiler can answer it at build time. Probe b is the UNSIGNED wrap, which IS a guarantee even in c++ (and in rust is spelled wrapping_add). Probe c is rust's explicit wrapping_add, which must hold in BOTH build modes -- the guarantee, as against the mode-dependent default. cpp signed overflow expects <any>, per the owner's cpp-UB ruling: probed for evidence, but there is no promise to break.

What `/` answers between two integers. Float camp: python typescript php dart. Truncate-toward-zero camp: rust go java csharp kotlin cpp (dart spells it ~/). Floor camp: ruby. Probe c is the separately-spelled integer division where one exists: python's // FLOORS (-4), dart's ~/ TRUNCATES (-3), ruby's .div FLOORS (-4).

The sign of modulo. Divisor-sign (floor-mod) camp: python, ruby. Dividend-sign (truncating remainder) camp: rust go java csharp kotlin cpp dart typescript. The census does not place php; this run places it. Probe c is the both-positive sanity case, which no camp disagrees about. The census does not place php on this fracture, so php's cell RECORDS its answer rather than checking it, and the answer is carried into the log as a proposed census addition.

Integer division (and modulo) by zero. Refuse camp: python ruby java csharp kotlin go(panic) rust(panic) dart(throws) php8(throws). Undefined behaviour: cpp. Infinity/NaN: typescript, which never had an integer. Isolated in its own program because c++'s answer on this machine is a signal that ends the process.

Bit operations and their width. Declared-width camp: rust go java csharp kotlin cpp dart-native -- probe a shifts inside a 32-bit declared type (answer -2147483648) and probe b inside a 64-bit one (answer 4294967296), which together are what 'on the declared width' MEANS. Unbounded camp: python ruby (and php, whose int is 64-bit) -- probe a grows to 2147483648. typescript coerces to 32 bits regardless, so probe b answers 1: the famous surprise.
